 West Coast faces heavy rain, powerful surf as atmospheric river fuels season's most relentless, intense storms
 The most significant threat this week will be along the coastlines of Washington, Oregon and California, where massive ocean swells will drive destructive surf and life-threatening sneaker waves.
 By
 Hayley Vawter 
 Source
 FOX Weather
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email 
 Copy Link
 02:01 Strong storms continue to rattle Northwest US 
 Intense atmospheric rivers are moving onshore in the Pacific Northwest, bringing dangerous waves, gusty winds and even snow, especially to Washington and Oregon. Conditions are impacting as far south as Northern California. Get the forecast: 
 THE TAKEAWAY  
 Storms will continue in the Pacific Northwest through mid-week. 
 The biggest threats are damaging winds, intense and dangerous surf and snow for the higher elevations. 
 Widespread rain will keep soaking the already-saturated ground, and totals are likely to exceed 6 inches in some places along the coasts. 
 The Pacific Northwest has faced a week of storms that've brought near tropical storm-force winds , rounds of heavy rain, massive waves and even snow, all of which will continue through mid-week. 
 The most significant threat this week will be along the coastlines of Washington , Oregon and California , where massive ocean swells will drive destructive surf and life-threatening sneaker waves, the FOX Forecast Center said. 
 Top rainfall reports
 (FOX Weather) 
  A broader, much stronger system in the northeast Pacific is sweeping a front onshore through Saturday.
 Widespread rain will keep soaking the already-saturated ground, and totals are likely to exceed 6 inches in some places along the coasts. 
 HERE'S WHAT TO DO IF YOU ENCOUNTER A FLOODED ROAD 
 Areas in and around San Francisco have reported flash flooding, with water covering roads and vehicles trapped in flooding . 
 SAN FRANCISCO, CA - NOVEMBER 3: A view of Golden Gate Bridge as big waves are seen during a rainy day at Fort Point in San Francisco, California, United States on November 3, 2026. 
 (Tayfun Coskun/Anadolu  / Getty Images) 
 Winds between 60 and 80 mph will be a problem along the coast, and 40 mph along the Interstate 5 corridor, the FOX Forecast Center said. 
 High Wind Warnings are also in place across the south-central Oregon coast. 
 High Surf Warnings and Advisories are in place today along the OR and SW WA coast through Saturday. Large waves and dangerous surf conditions with breakers up to 30-35 ft are expected. High surf will produce rip currents & sneaker waves. Stay off the beach! https://t.co/7244ZSZeMj
— NWS Portland (@NWSPortland)  November 13, 2026 This weekend's storms are part of a much larger pattern. 
 The FOX Forecast Center said each of these storms will be powerful, fueling even higher winds over the Pacific pushing monster waves toward the coast.
 FROM CALM TO CHAOS: SNEAKER WAVES TURN BEACH VISITS INTO LIFE-OR-DEATH STRUGGLES IN SECONDS 
 Massive waves between 40 and 50 mph are possible through Monday along the Washington, Oregon and Northern California coasts. 
 Sunday night wave height forecast
 (FOX Weather) 
  High Surf Warmings are in place for these areas through the weekend. 
 San Francisco also is in a Coastal Flood Advisory through Saturday evening. 
 THANKSGIVING WEATHER NIGHTMARES: A LOOK BACK AT THE MOST POWERFUL HOLIDAY STORMS IN US HISTORY 
 Beach erosion will threaten more than 500 miles of coastline from Washington to Southern California, the FOX Forecast Center said. 
 Rain forecast
 (FOX Weather) 
  Turning to the Sierra Nevada and Intermountain West, snow will be the main event. 
 A large ridge of upper-level high pressure is building across the interior West, acting like a wall against the broader Pacific storm track instead of allowing these systems to cleanly move inland. 
 It started on Friday, as an atmospheric river was split in two pieces, and heavy rain will push into Northern and Central California and snow and strong winds will push into the Sierra Nevada. 
 HOW TO WATCH FOX WEATHER 
 SNow forecast West
 (FOX Weather) 
  A Winter Storm Warning is in effect for areas including parts of Yosemite National Park and the Eastern Sierra mountains. 
 Snow is forecast to remain between 5,000 and 7,000 feet elevation.
